{
  "project_id": "P-AFW-HealthSecurityPhase3",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Escalating conflict and violence in the region may disrupt project activities, limit access to target areas and endanger staff.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Maintain security liaison, develop flexible implementation plans, pre‑position supplies, and activate contingency protocols with local authorities.",
      "evidence": "Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence… regional conflicts, such as Boko Haram attacks in Cameroon and ongoing unrest in CAR (Section A2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Delays in recruiting required PIU specialists (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) could stall project start‑up.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Launch early recruitment drives, use temporary contracts, and provide incentives to attract qualified staff before the effectiveness date.",
      "evidence": "Recipient shall appoint, assign, or recruit an accountant, a knowledge management… specialist no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date (Legal Covenants)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Weak financial management capacity leads to inaccurate reporting, misallocation of funds and audit findings.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Update FM manuals, customize accounting software, recruit internal and external auditors, and provide World Bank‑led FM training and supervision.",
      "evidence": "The overall FM residual risk rating is Substantial… FM risk assessment at concept for the project… rated as Substantial (Section 58‑59)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Procurement delays, weak contract management and limited market competition in fragile settings may cause cost overruns and schedule slips.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, use STEP for real‑time monitoring, and strengthen contract‑management training.",
      "evidence": "Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management… mitigation measures include hiring experienced procurement specialists (Section 64‑65)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Construction and civil works generate waste, dust, emissions and occupational hazards that could affect nearby communities.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Prepare site‑specific ESMPs, enforce waste‑management plans, monitor air quality and provide PPE to workers.",
      "evidence": "Environmental risks are considered Substantial… impacts on water quality; disposal of building/construction wastes; occupational health and safety (Section 66)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Increased community health workforce raises risk of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH).",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct GBV/SEA risk assessments, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, train all staff on codes of conduct and establish reporting mechanisms.",
      "evidence": "Overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial… increased presence of new health workforce such as CHWs may create concerns of Sexual exploitation and abuse (Section 72‑73)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Climate change will increase vector‑borne diseases and flood‑related outbreaks, stressing health services and facilities.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate‑resilient designs in health infrastructure, embed climate data into surveillance systems, and develop climate‑adaptation response plans.",
      "evidence": "Climate change contributed to at least 50 % of natural disasters… increasing temperatures expanding malaria‑transmitting mosquitoes (Section 11)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Low domestic health financing and high out‑of‑pocket spending threaten long‑term sustainability of interventions.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Support domestic resource mobilization, integrate health security into national budgets, and assist governments in developing medium‑term expenditure frameworks.",
      "evidence": "Cameroon’s domestic funding for health per capita was US$10.79… high reliance on out‑of‑pocket payments (61 %) (Annex 2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Governance weaknesses at national level may slow decision‑making and impede coordinated implementation.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen steering committees, provide governance capacity‑building, and establish clear reporting lines and timelines.",
      "evidence": "Key risks to successful implementation… governance challenges, economic constraints, and environmental vulnerabilities (Section 16)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Failure to sign the MoU with WOAH within 90 days could limit regional animal health coordination.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set internal deadline reminders, monitor compliance, and engage legal support to expedite MoU finalisation.",
      "evidence": "Recipient shall, no later than ninety (90) days after the Effective Date, enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with WOAH (Legal Covenants)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Disruptions in global supply chains may delay delivery of vaccines, diagnostics and PPE needed for emergencies.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish buffer stocks, diversify suppliers, and develop logistics contingency plans with regional hubs.",
      "evidence": "Support to access countermeasures through strengthening emergency logistics and supply chains, including stockpiling (Component 3.1)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Fragmented data systems across human, animal and environmental sectors hinder real‑time surveillance and decision‑making.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop an interoperable digital platform, adopt common data standards, and train staff on integrated use of DHIS2 and LIMS.",
      "evidence": "Developing interoperable digital platform… integration of OH data using DHIS2 (Annex 1, Subcomponent 2.1)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Under‑representation of women in technical epidemiology and veterinary roles limits gender‑responsive capacity.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set gender quotas, conduct outreach to female candidates, and provide flexible training formats.",
      "evidence": "Women remain underrepresented… project targets women training in FETP and veterinary fields (Section 75‑76)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Inadequate stakeholder engagement may exclude vulnerable groups, leading to grievances and project delays.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement robust GRM, conduct inclusive consultations, and adapt the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan to national contexts.",
      "evidence": "Potential exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups… citizen engagement mechanisms such as consultations and GRMs (Section 71‑74)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Security threats to staff operating in FCV zones could cause injuries or evacuation, halting activities.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prepare country‑specific Security Risk Assessments and Management Plans, provide security training and insurance, and adjust field schedules as needed.",
      "evidence": "PIUs of FCV countries will also prepare a country‑specific Security Risk Assessment (SRA) and Security Risk Management Plan (SMP) (Section 73)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Customising existing accounting software after the effectiveness date may be delayed, affecting financial reporting.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Award IT contract early, set milestone‑based delivery schedule, and conduct user‑acceptance testing before go‑live.",
      "evidence": "Customize the existing accounting software… no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date (Legal Covenants)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "High turnover of health workers due to displacement and insecurity reduces programme continuity.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Offer retention incentives, remote training options, and establish backup staffing pools.",
      "evidence": "Over 1.5 million IDPs and refugees… internal displacement affecting health workforce (Section 3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Poor quality or untimely M&E data could impede performance tracking and decision‑making.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen M&E capacity, conduct regular data quality audits, and use standardized reporting templates.",
      "evidence": "PIUs will be responsible for M&E… ensure data harmonized and comparable (Section B)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "Inadequate biosafety in laboratories may cause accidental pathogen exposure or contamination.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement biosafety training, certify labs to SLIPTA standards, and enforce strict SOPs for sample handling.",
      "evidence": "Laboratory Quality and Capacity subcomponent includes biosafety & biosecurity (Section 30)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R20",
      "description": "Non‑compliance with ESF safeguards could trigger World Bank suspensions or project delays.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Finalize ESCP, LMP and SEP early, conduct regular E&S monitoring, and remediate any non‑compliance promptly.",
      "evidence": "Project prepared under ESF… environmental risks substantial… site‑specific ESMPs required (Section 65‑66)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R21",
      "description": "Macroeconomic instability may limit government ability to meet co‑financing commitments.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Negotiate flexible financing arrangements, maintain contingency reserves, and coordinate with development partners for supplemental funding.",
      "evidence": "Challenging macro‑fiscal outlook and high poverty levels make the region vulnerable to shocks (Section A2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R22",
      "description": "Procurement fraud or corruption could erode trust and waste resources.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply World Bank Anti‑Fraud and Corruption Guidelines, conduct independent audits, and enforce strict vendor vetting.",
      "evidence": "Procurement will follow World Bank Procurement Regulations… Anti‑Fraud and Corruption Guidelines (Section 62)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R23",
      "description": "Delay in preparing the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) manual and emergency action plan may hinder rapid fund deployment.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop CERC manual and EAP within the first six months, obtain Bank approval early, and train staff on activation procedures.",
      "evidence": "CERC component… Government will prepare a CERC Manual, submit an emergency action plan (Section 35)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R24",
      "description": "Weak coordination among multiple ministries and agencies can cause duplication and inefficiencies.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish clear terms of reference for the National Steering Committee and Technical Committee, and hold regular joint coordination meetings.",
      "evidence": "Implementation under respective Ministries… PIU will coordinate… national steering committee and technical committee will oversee (Section 44‑45)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R25",
      "description": "Improper handling of medical and laboratory waste may contaminate the environment and pose health hazards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt the National Healthcare Waste Management Plan, train staff on waste segregation, and monitor disposal practices.",
      "evidence": "Project will take advantage of the existing National Healthcare Waste Management Plan… (Section 23)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Escalating conflict and violence in the region may disrupt project activities, limit access to target areas and endanger staff.
risks.mitigation: Maintain security liaison, develop flexible implementation plans, pre‑position supplies, and activate contingency protocols with local authorities.
risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence… regional conflicts, such as Boko Haram attacks in Cameroon and ongoing unrest in CAR (Section A2).

risks.description: Delays in recruiting required PIU specialists (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) could stall project start‑up.
risks.mitigation: Launch early recruitment drives, use temporary contracts, and provide incentives to attract qualified staff before the effectiveness date.
risks.evidence: Recipient shall appoint, assign, or recruit an accountant, a knowledge management… specialist no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date (Legal Covenants).

risks.description: Weak financial management capacity leads to inaccurate reporting, misallocation of funds and audit findings.
risks.mitigation: Update FM manuals, customize accounting software, recruit internal and external auditors, and provide World Bank‑led FM training and supervision.
risks.evidence: The overall FM residual risk rating is Substantial… FM risk assessment at concept for the project… rated as Substantial (Section 58‑59).

risks.description: Procurement delays, weak contract management and limited market competition in fragile settings may cause cost overruns and schedule slips.
risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, use STEP for real‑time monitoring, and strengthen contract‑management training.
risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management… mitigation measures include hiring experienced procurement specialists (Section 64‑65).

risks.mitigation: Prepare site‑specific ESMPs, enforce waste‑management plans, monitor air quality and provide PPE to workers.

risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV/SEA risk assessments, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, train all staff on codes of conduct and establish reporting mechanisms.
risks.evidence: Overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial… increased presence of new health workforce such as CHWs may create concerns of Sexual exploitation and abuse (Section 72‑73).

risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient designs in health infrastructure, embed climate data into surveillance systems, and develop climate‑adaptation response plans.
risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 % of natural disasters… increasing temperatures expanding malaria‑transmitting mosquitoes (Section 11).

risks.mitigation: Support domestic resource mobilization, integrate health security into national budgets, and assist governments in developing medium‑term expenditure frameworks.
risks.evidence: Cameroon’s domestic funding for health per capita was US$10.79… high reliance on out‑of‑pocket payments (61 %) (Annex 2).

risks.description: Governance weaknesses at national level may slow decision‑making and impede coordinated implementation.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen steering committees, provide governance capacity‑building, and establish clear reporting lines and timelines.

risks.evidence: Support to access countermeasures through strengthening emergency logistics and supply chains, including stockpiling (Component 3.1).

risks.description: Fragmented data systems across human, animal and environmental sectors hinder real‑time surveillance and decision‑making.
risks.mitigation: Develop an interoperable digital platform, adopt common data standards, and train staff on integrated use of DHIS2 and LIMS.
risks.evidence: Developing interoperable digital platform… integration of OH data using DHIS2 (Annex 1, Subcomponent 2.1).

risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement may exclude vulnerable groups, leading to grievances and project delays.
risks.mitigation: Implement robust GRM, conduct inclusive consultations, and adapt the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan to national contexts.

risks.evidence: PIUs of FCV countries will also prepare a country‑specific Security Risk Assessment (SRA) and Security Risk Management Plan (SMP) (Section 73).

risks.description: Customising existing accounting software after the effectiveness date may be delayed, affecting financial reporting.
risks.mitigation: Award IT contract early, set milestone‑based delivery schedule, and conduct user‑acceptance testing before go‑live.
risks.evidence: Customize the existing accounting software… no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date (Legal Covenants).

risks.description: High turnover of health workers due to displacement and insecurity reduces programme continuity.
risks.mitigation: Offer retention incentives, remote training options, and establish backup staffing pools.
risks.evidence: Over 1.5 million IDPs and refugees… internal displacement affecting health workforce (Section 3).

risks.description: Poor quality or untimely M&E data could impede performance tracking and decision‑making.

risks.evidence: PIUs will be responsible for M&E… ensure data harmonized and comparable (Section B).

risks.description: Inadequate biosafety in laboratories may cause accidental pathogen exposure or contamination.
risks.mitigation: Implement biosafety training, certify labs to SLIPTA standards, and enforce strict SOPs for sample handling.
risks.evidence: Laboratory Quality and Capacity subcomponent includes biosafety & biosecurity (Section 30).

risks.description: Non‑compliance with ESF safeguards could trigger World Bank suspensions or project delays.
risks.mitigation: Finalize ESCP, LMP and SEP early, conduct regular E&S monitoring, and remediate any non‑compliance promptly.
risks.evidence: Project prepared under ESF… environmental risks substantial… site‑specific ESMPs required (Section 65‑66).

risks.description: Macroeconomic instability may limit government ability to meet co‑financing commitments.
risks.mitigation: Negotiate flexible financing arrangements, maintain contingency reserves, and coordinate with development partners for supplemental funding.
risks.evidence: Challenging macro‑fiscal outlook and high poverty levels make the region vulnerable to shocks (Section A2).

risks.description: Procurement fraud or corruption could erode trust and waste resources.
risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank Anti‑Fraud and Corruption Guidelines, conduct independent audits, and enforce strict vendor vetting.
risks.evidence: Procurement will follow World Bank Procurement Regulations… Anti‑Fraud and Corruption Guidelines (Section 62).

risks.description: Delay in preparing the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) manual and emergency action plan may hinder rapid fund deployment.
risks.mitigation: Develop CERC manual and EAP within the first six months, obtain Bank approval early, and train staff on activation procedures.
risks.evidence: CERC component… Government will prepare a CERC Manual, submit an emergency action plan (Section 35).

risks.description: Weak coordination among multiple ministries and agencies can cause duplication and inefficiencies.
risks.mitigation: Establish clear terms of reference for the National Steering Committee and Technical Committee, and hold regular joint coordination meetings.
risks.evidence: Implementation under respective Ministries… PIU will coordinate… national steering committee and technical committee will oversee (Section 44‑45).

risks.description: Improper handling of medical and laboratory waste may contaminate the environment and pose health hazards.
risks.mitigation: Adopt the National Healthcare Waste Management Plan, train staff on waste segregation, and monitor disposal practices.
risks.evidence: Project will take advantage of the existing National Healthcare Waste Management Plan… (Section 23).
